claims.text: The POL-RD-01 establishment test is met on this trip's own trace. The governing measure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 14.4 km, against a booked optimal distance of 9.0 km stored on the trip record at booking. The excess is 5.4 km, which is 60.0% of optimal. Both gates pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. A route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on the trace, and the trip_record.actual_distance_km figure of 14.4 km is not needed for the test because the clause makes the trace figure govern.

The deviation is not merely established but MATERIAL: the excess is 60.0% of optimal, above the 50% materiality gate (the 8.0 km absolute gate is not reached, but only one limb is needed). Materiality is assessed on the excess remaining after any adjustment under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12, and for the reasons given below no adjustment applies, so the excess remains 5.4 km at 60.0%. That materiality finding is what requires the driver_profile check under POL-RD-06.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the deviation may rest on it alone and no corroboration is required. It carries 114 fixes at a 10 second sample interval (the clause's ceiling is a sustained interval above 30 seconds), max_gap_sec is 0.0 with an empty gaps list (the clause's threshold is a gap above 90 seconds), and coverage is 100.0%. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and the rider's burden under POL-RD-08(b) is discharged from the trace itself.

The rider carries and has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. First, the artifacts describe the same trip: EV-TRIP-02851, EV-GPS-02851 and EV-FARE-02851 all carry trip identifier TRP-02851, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-23T19:19:43+08:00 matches the trip record's recorded trip_started event to the minute. Second, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold — 5.4 km at 60.0% — is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The rider's own profile carries deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the additional-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 for low-substantiation claimants is not triggered.

The driver's counterparty_statement — 'Road works.' — does not discharge the shifted burden and must be discarded. It names no evidence id for any advisory, and the only traffic-advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02851-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (its absence is itself citable). I disclose that impairment expressly: this artifact can carry no fact. With no advisory on file, POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all — there is no record naming a road the optimal route traverses, no validity window and no alternative-route distance — so the exoneration is unavailable and, under POL-RD-08, a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory id, carries no weight. Under POL-RD-13 the deviation then stands at the measured figure.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of this excess. The chat log for this trip is COMPLETE, holds 0 messages, and has null first_message_at and last_message_at; the trip record likewise records chat_message_count of 0. There is therefore no rider instruction, no timestamp before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and no chat_message.waypoint_hint within the meaning of POL-RD-04, whose waypoint correlation test cannot even be run. The clause is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded from the excess.

No relocation exoneration applies. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. With no amendment timestamp and no stored re-quote, POL-RD-05 does not run and no substitute amended optimal may be derived from the record, so the 9.0 km booked optimal remains the baseline for the POL-RD-01 test.

The pooled-itinerary baseline does not apply either. The vehicle_type on the trip record is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 therefore has no work to do, and the 9.0 km matched figure the rider's claim is measured against is the correct booked optimal.

The distance-and-time remedy is not closed off by the upfront-pricing clause. EV-FARE-02851 records fare_model as METERED and quoted_fare_sgd as null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs the refund computation on the booked optimal route.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic on the booked optimal route is: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 9.0 + 0.28 x 13.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = (3.80 + 6.75 + 3.64) + 0.80 = 14.99; charged_total = 20.66; refund = 20.66 - 14.99 = 5.67, payable rounded up to 5.70. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the de minimis NO_ACTION does not apply. The surge_multiplier of 1.0 is read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN, where the clause places it and where it is the only place it lives.

Because a MATERIAL deviation is substantiated on this trip's own evidence, and because driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3 — at or above the 3-flag threshold in POL-RD-06 — a repeat deviation pattern is ESTABLISHED. The alternative ratio limb is not needed (3/180 is below 0.05) but the flag limb is independently satisfied. Under POL-RD-06(b) the remedy is therefore FULL_REFUND of charged_total, 20.66, rather than the POL-RD-02 partial of 5.67, and the ruling must state the POL-RD-02 figure and the uplifted figure side by side so the size of the uplift is visible. For POL-GEN-01 compliance I use only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d for this test; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (5) is NOT the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for and I do not rely on it.

Nothing in the fare has to be carved out of that FULL_REFUND figure. The fare breakdown carries erp_gantries as an empty list and an ERP total of 0.00, no airport surcharge line (and this trip does not originate at an airport), waiting_time_fee of 0.0 and promo_discount of 0.0. POL-RD-09 therefore adds nothing on top and subtracts nothing from the refund: the full contested amount of 20.66 is refundable to the rider.

The rider also asks for the POL-RD-06(c) referral to driver-conduct review, which follows automatically from the established pattern. That referral is an addition to the monetary ruling, not a substitute for it: under POL-GEN-03 a referral never suppresses the money, and the refund issues regardless of the conduct review.

No escalation trigger fires and the rider asks the Judge to rule on the money rather than hold it. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; no timestamps run backwards or disagree; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; and the POL-RD-02 refund of 5.67 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, so POL-RD-10(6) is not engaged. POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged either, because the driver cited no advisory identifier at all: under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an advisory no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it.

The outcome is party-relative and the rider is the filing party. The dispute was filed by RIDER, the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.0, so the present payment state is that the rider has paid the full contested 20.66. A refund ruling moves that money back to the rider; NO_ACTION would leave the whole 20.66 with the platform. On this record the rider should not be left carrying the disputed charge.

claims.text: The only distance figure that governs the POL-RD-01 test is the trace, and on this record the trace is clean: 114 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a zero-second maximum gap, so the measurement is not contestable. The excess is therefore exactly what the code derived from that trace — 5.4 km over the 9.0 km optimal route, 60% — and that measured excess, not the rider's characterisation of the whole fare, is the outer limit of what the rider has shown on this trip.

Where the deviation stands, POL-RD-02 prices it arithmetically and not by the rider's assertion. Applying the clause to the stored optimal route: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 9.0 km + 0.28 x 13.0 min) at the surge multiplier of 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else, plus the 0.80 platform fee and no ERP, gives a recomputed fare of SGD 14.99 against SGD 20.66 charged — a refund of SGD 5.67, rounded up to SGD 5.70, which is 27.4% of the charge and far below the 90% that would make it a full refund. The most the rider can recover on this record under POL-RD-02 is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.70.

The rider contests the entire SGD 20.66, but POL-RD-02 returns only the difference between the charge and the metered cost of the optimal route; it does not return the SGD 3.80 base fare, the SGD 0.80 platform fee, or the time charge for the 18.8 minutes actually driven. POL-GEN-03 defines a PARTIAL_REFUND as part of the contested amount, not all of it, and apart from the POL-RD-06 uplift addressed separately below nothing on this record licenses returning the whole charge.

Every charge line on the fare ledger has a counterpart and there is nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure: the ERP lines are empty, there is no airport surcharge (this trip neither originates at nor ends at an airport), the waiting-time fee is zero and there is no promo discount. POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding off-route ERP a second time on top of the POL-RD-02 refund, and with no unmatched gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge there is no billing-integrity line for POL-RD-09(4) to bite on.

The POL-RD-06 pattern test, if it is met at all, is met only by its absolute-count limb: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, exactly the clause's floor value, while the ratio limb is nowhere near — 3 over driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 180 is 1.67%, against the 5% the clause requires. The limb (b) uplift to a full refund is a deterrent aimed at the serial long-hauler, and the same citable profile shows a driver who completed 180 trips in the trailing window at a flag rate well under the clause's own 5% signal; the judge should price this trip under POL-RD-02 at SGD 5.70 rather than uplift it to the full SGD 20.66.

The driver's account of this detour has been road works from the outset, and the artifact that would test that account is not in the bundle at all: EV-ADVIS-02851-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, which the driver discloses. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run on the record, and under POL-RD-10(5) an exculpatory closure asserted with no traffic_advisory is a mandatory escalation rather than a monetary ruling — a consequence POL-RD-13(1) expressly preserves where the missing identifier is cited, as it is cited here. On the driver's case the disputed amount should be held for the human reviewer, not refunded on an untested record.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 20.66 charged for trip TRP-02851 is refunded in full to the rider, and the case is sent for driver-conduct review. Why, step by step.

1. The detour is proved, and it is a material one. The distance that governs is the GPS trace EV-GPS-02851 — 14.4 km — and not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record, because POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern. The booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-02851 is 9.0 km. The excess is 5.4 km, or 60.0% of optimal: above both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km and 20%) and above the 50% that makes the deviation MATERIAL. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 114 fixes at 10-second intervals, maximum gap 0.0 s, empty gaps list, 100% coverage — so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) do not fire and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: the trip id TRP-02851 matches across EV-TRIP-02851, EV-GPS-02851 and EV-FARE-02851, and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace.

2. Nothing reduces the excess. The chat log EV-CHAT-02851 holds 0 messages, so there is no rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04); no pickup or dropoff amendment was made (POL-RD-05); the vehicle was RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12). The driver's explanation, 'Road works.', names no advisory evidence ID, and no traffic advisory is on file: EV-ADVIS-02851-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. That artifact carries no fact and its absence is all it evidences; it discounts nothing here. Without a record naming a road the optimal route traverses, a validity window and an alternative-route length, POL-RD-03 cannot be run, so the traffic assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure. The assertion is discarded and no advisory was on file. That materiality finding is what requires the driver_profile check under POL-RD-06.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the deviation may rest on it alone and no corroboration is required. It carries 114 fixes at a 10 second sample interval (the clause's ceiling is a sustained interval above 30 seconds), max_gap_sec is 0.0 with an empty gaps list (the clause's threshold is a gap above 90 seconds), and coverage is 100.0%. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and the rider's burden under POL-RD-08(b) is discharged from the trace itself.

The rider carries and has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. First, the artifacts describe the same trip: EV-TRIP-02851, EV-GPS-02851 and EV-FARE-02851 all carry trip identifier TRP-02851, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-23T19:19:43+08:00 matches the trip record's recorded trip_started event to the minute. Second, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold — 5.4 km at 60.0% — is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The rider's own profile carries deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the additional-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 for low-substantiation claimants is not triggered.

The driver's counterparty_statement — 'Road works.' — does not discharge the shifted burden and must be discarded. It names no evidence id for any advisory, and the only traffic-advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02851-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (its absence is itself citable). I disclose that impairment expressly: this artifact can carry no fact. With no advisory on file, POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all — there is no record naming a road the optimal route traverses, no validity window and no alternative-route distance — so the exoneration is unavailable and, under POL-RD-08, a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory id, carries no weight. Under POL-RD-13 the deviation then stands at the measured figure.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of this excess. The chat log for this trip is COMPLETE, holds 0 messages, and has null first_message_at and last_message_at; the trip record likewise records chat_message_count of 0. There is therefore no rider instruction, no timestamp before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and no chat_message.waypoint_hint within the meaning of POL-RD-04, whose waypoint correlation test cannot even be run. The clause is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded from the excess.

No relocation exoneration applies. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. With no amendment timestamp and no stored re-quote, POL-RD-05 does not run and no substitute amended optimal may be derived from the record, so the 9.0 km booked optimal remains the baseline for the POL-RD-01 test.

The pooled-itinerary baseline does not apply either. The vehicle_type on the trip record is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 therefore has no work to do, and the 9.0 km matched figure the rider's claim is measured against is the correct booked optimal.

The distance-and-time remedy is not closed off by the upfront-pricing clause. EV-FARE-02851 records fare_model as METERED and quoted_fare_sgd as null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs the refund computation on the booked optimal route.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic on the booked optimal route is: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 9.0 + 0.28 x 13.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = (3.80 + 6.75 + 3.64) + 0.80 = 14.99; charged_total = 20.66; refund = 20.66 - 14.99 = 5.67, payable rounded up to 5.70. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the de minimis NO_ACTION does not apply. The surge_multiplier of 1.0 is read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN, where the clause places it and where it is the only place it lives.

Because a MATERIAL deviation is substantiated on this trip's own evidence, and because driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3 — at or above the 3-flag threshold in POL-RD-06 — a repeat deviation pattern is ESTABLISHED. The alternative ratio limb is not needed (3/180 is below 0.05) but the flag limb is independently satisfied. Under POL-RD-06(b) the remedy is therefore FULL_REFUND of charged_total, 20.66, rather than the POL-RD-02 partial of 5.67, and the ruling must state the POL-RD-02 figure and the uplifted figure side by side so the size of the uplift is visible. For POL-GEN-01 compliance I use only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d for this test; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (5) is NOT the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for and I do not rely on it.

ledger.claim: Nothing in the fare has to be carved out of that FULL_REFUND figure. The fare breakdown carries erp_gantries as an empty list and an ERP total of 0.00, no airport surcharge line (and this trip does not originate at an airport), waiting_time_fee of 0.0 and promo_discount of 0.0. POL-RD-09 therefore adds nothing on top and subtracts nothing from the refund: the full contested amount of 20.66 is refundable to the rider.

The rider also asks for the POL-RD-06(c) referral to driver-conduct review, which follows automatically from the established pattern. That referral is an addition to the monetary ruling, not a substitute for it: under POL-GEN-03 a referral never suppresses the money, and the refund issues regardless of the conduct review.

No escalation trigger fires and the rider asks the Judge to rule on the money rather than hold it. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; no timestamps run backwards or disagree; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; and the POL-RD-02 refund of 5.67 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, so POL-RD-10(6) is not engaged. POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged either, because the driver cited no advisory identifier at all: under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an advisory no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it.

ledger.claim: The outcome is party-relative and the rider is the filing party. The dispute was filed by RIDER, the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.0, so the present payment state is that the rider has paid the full contested 20.66. A refund ruling moves that money back to the rider; NO_ACTION would leave the whole 20.66 with the platform. On this record the rider should not be left carrying the disputed charge.

The only distance figure that governs the POL-RD-01 test is the trace, and on this record the trace is clean: 114 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a zero-second maximum gap, so the measurement is not contestable. The excess is therefore exactly what the code derived from that trace — 5.4 km over the 9.0 km optimal route, 60% — and that measured excess, not the rider's characterisation of the whole fare, is the outer limit of what the rider has shown on this trip.

Where the deviation stands, POL-RD-02 prices it arithmetically and not by the rider's assertion. Applying the clause to the stored optimal route: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 9.0 km + 0.28 x 13.0 min) at the surge multiplier of 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else, plus the 0.80 platform fee and no ERP, gives a recomputed fare of SGD 14.99 against SGD 20.66 charged — a refund of SGD 5.67, rounded up to SGD 5.70, which is 27.4% of the charge and far below the 90% that would make it a full refund. The most the rider can recover on this record under POL-RD-02 is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.70.

The rider contests the entire SGD 20.66, but POL-RD-02 returns only the difference between the charge and the metered cost of the optimal route; it does not return the SGD 3.80 base fare, the SGD 0.80 platform fee, or the time charge for the 18.8 minutes actually driven. POL-GEN-03 defines a PARTIAL_REFUND as part of the contested amount, not all of it, and apart from the POL-RD-06 uplift addressed separately below nothing on this record licenses returning the whole charge.

Every charge line on the fare ledger has a counterpart and there is nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure: the ERP lines are empty, there is no airport surcharge (this trip neither originates at nor ends at an airport), the waiting-time fee is zero and there is no promo discount. POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding off-route ERP a second time on top of the POL-RD-02 refund, and with no unmatched gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge there is no billing-integrity line for POL-RD-09(4) to bite on.

The POL-RD-06 pattern test, if it is met at all, is met only by its absolute-count limb: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, exactly the clause's floor value, while the ratio limb is nowhere near — 3 over driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 180 is 1.67%, against the 5% the clause requires. The limb (b) uplift to a full refund is a deterrent aimed at the serial long-hauler, and the same citable profile shows a driver who completed 180 trips in the trailing window at a flag rate well under the clause's own 5% signal; the judge should price this trip under POL-RD-02 at SGD 5.70 rather than uplift it to the full SGD 20.66.

The driver's account of this detour has been road works from the outset, and the artifact that would test that account is not in the bundle at all: EV-ADVIS-02851-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, which the driver discloses. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run on the record, and under POL-RD-10(5) an exculpatory closure asserted with no traffic_advisory is a mandatory escalation rather than a monetary ruling — a consequence POL-RD-13(1) expressly preserves where the missing identifier is cited, as it is cited here. On the driver's case the disputed amount should be held for the human reviewer, not refunded on an untested record.
